questions.explanation: Candidates are required to state that; Peter refers to Christian leaders as witnesses of the suffering of Christ and partakers of the glory that is to be revealed during his second coming. They should therefore look after the flock of Christ with tenderness. They should not regard their assignment as a burden rather they should discharge their duties willingly. Not for shameful material gain but eagerly. Not by being overbearing but serving as true examples/role model to the flock. They would reap their due reward in due course when the Lord comes. Leaders should humble themselves under the mighty hand of God for God to exalt them. They must be sober and watchful because Satan is roaming around looking for whom to destroy. They should resist Satan at all costs and be firm in their faith. Suffering is part of the Christian life. God will reward them for their role. Love the brotherhood. Keep a clear conscience so that they can put to shame those who abuse them. He also admonished the younger ones in the church to be subject to the elders. According to Peter, Christians should clothe themselves with humility towards one another. Peter also advised Christians to resist the devil and he would flee from them/ they could resist the devil with their faith in Christ. Finally, they should stand firm in their faith, for the enemy was always seeking an opportunity to attack.

questions.question:
SECTION A: THEMES FROM THE OLD TESTAMENT

 
Relate to how marriage was instituted by God in the second creation story.
questions.explanation: Below are the expected points from candidates; 1. In the second creation story, God created man out of dust and gave him breath to become a living being. 2. God placed man in the garden of Eden to keep and till it. 3. So He created all living creatures and charged man to name them but none was fit as a partner for him. 4. God saw that man was lonely. 5. God, therefore, said that it was not good for man to be alone. 6. Hence He decided to make a helper fit for man as his partner. 7. God caused a deep sleep to fall upon man. 8. And while the man slept, He took one of his ribs and closed up its place with flesh. 9. And out of the rib God took from man, He made a woman and brought her to the man. 10. When the man saw the woman, he said, “This, at last, is bone of my bones and flesh of my flesh...”. 11. Man said, she shall be called woman because she was taken out of man. 12. That day, man and woman became married couple. 13. Hence a man leaves his father and mother and cleaves to his wife and they become one flesh. 14. And the man and his wife were both naked and were not ashamed.

questions.question:
SECTION A: THEMES FROM THE OLD TESTAMENT

 
Recount the effects of the behaviour of Eli’s children on Israel as a nation (1 Samuel 2:12-36, 3:2-18, 4:10-22).
questions.explanation: Expected answers are highlighted below on the consequences of the behaviours of Eli’s children on Israel; 1. God sent the Philistines to fight Israel. 2. Israel was defeated though she went to war with the ark of God. 3. About three thousand Israelites died in the war. 4. The ark of the covenant was also captured by the Philistines. 5. The two sons of Eli were also killed. 6. Eli died when he heard that his two sons were dead and the ark also captured. 7. When Phinehas’ wife, who was pregnant heard of the death of her husband and the father-in-law, she gave birth prematurely and later died. 8. The child that was born was called Ichabod, meaning, “The glory has departed from Israel.” 9. Thus the priestly position of Eli was taken away from the family.

questions.question:
SECTION A: THEMES FROM THE OLD TESTAMENT

 
(a)      Highlight the religious tension in Israel during the reign of King Ahab
(b)      Identify three steps that can be taken to minimize religious tension in the society.
questions.explanation: (A) Religious tension in Israel during the reign of King Ahab. (I kings 16:29-34, 17:1-7, 18: 1-19) In regards to this question, candidates are expected to highlight the points as listed below; 1. Ahab married Jezebel, the daughter of Ethbaal, King of the Sidonians. 2. She was a staunch worshipper of Baal of Phoenicia. 3. Jezebel was allowed by Ahab to bring into Israel the worship of Baal together with several Baal prophets and Prophets of Asherah. 4. She tried making Baalism state religion of Israel. 5. In pursuance of her policy, she killed the prophets of God who opposed her. 6. The prophets of God who could not withstand Jezebel fled the country while others were hidden by Obadiah. 7. The altars of Yahweh were also cut down. 8. Ahab helped in the promotion of Baalism as he used state resources to build temples for Baal. 9. Ahab perpetrated grave social injustices during his reign eg. He had Naboth killed and took over his vineyard. 10. Many Israelites deserted Yahweh to worship Baal. 11. All these acts of idolatry and injustice incurred the displeasure of God. 12. It was around this time that Elijah from Tishbe, the prophet of God emerged to confront Ahab. 13. God asked Elijah to pronounce drought in Israel for three and a half years. 14. And as a result of the drought, there was severe famine on the land of Israel. 15. God used ravens to feed Elijah who went to hide by the brook Cherith from where he had water to drink. 16. For a while, Elijah was afraid to meet King Ahab for fear that Jezebel might kill him because she had earlier persecuted the prophets of Yahweh. 17. But after a while, the Lord told Elijah to present himself to King Ahab. 18. Ahab accused Elijah of being the troubler of Israel. 19. But Elijah maintained that it was Ahab and his royal house that had brought the drought because of their worship of Baal. 20. However, the tension was resolved by the contest on Mount Carmel, requested by Elijah. 21. The supremacy of God was established after Elijah won the contest. 22. Elijah then had the Baal prophets killed to reflect his victory over the Baal prophets. (B) Steps that can be taken to minimize religious tensions in society. 1. Tolerance/respect for the views of other religions/ avoid partiality/show love for all religions. 2. Have understanding and concern for others/ avoid derogatory remarks. 3. There should be inter-religious dialogue. 4. The state should recognize all religious faiths/freedom of worship. 5. Desist from greed and covetousness. 6. Do not tolerate evil counsel. 7. Focus on God only/fear God. 8. Sinners must be condemned. 9. Counselling people who go astray. 10. Men of God should speak against injustice/corruption, etc. 11. Using social media to expose evil deeds and doers in society. 12. Rights of citizens should be respected.

questions.question:
SECTION A: THEMES FROM THE OLD TESTAMENT

 
(A) How was greed demonstrated in the life of Gehazi?
 
(B) Give three areas in the society where greed is prevalent.
questions.explanation: (A) How greed was demonstrated in the life of Gehazi. (2 Kings 5:14-27) The points expected of candidates are; 1. After the cleansing of Naaman’s leprosy at river Jordan, he returned to the man of God (Elisha) with large amount of gifts. 2. He presented the gifts to Elisha the prophet, but he refused to accept them and dispatched him even after persuasion. 3. When Naaman had gone a short distance with his gifts, Gehazi, Elisha’s servant, followed him to request for the items his master had rejected. 4. Naaman saw him and alighted from his chariot to meet him. 5. He asked if all was well; Gehazi lied, saying that his master had sent him to collect the gifts. 6. Naaman gave Gehazi twice his request and ordered his servants to assist him to carry the items home. 7. He put them on two of his servants to carry them for Gehazi. 8. When they came close home he collected the items from them and sent the men away. 9. He then hid them in his room. 10. Later, his master Elisha got to know the misdeed of his servant and questioned him, ‘Where have you been, Gehazi?” 11. Gehazi lied that he went nowhere. 12. His master said he was with him in spirit and he saw the things he collected from Naaman. 13. He, therefore, cursed him that the leprosy of Naaman would cleave to him, and his descendants forever. 14. And it was so/ he became leprous immediately, as a result of his greed. In the B part, points expected of candidates include; 1. In the political circle - e.g. Legislative/Judiciary/Executive circles. 2. In business - e.g. profiteering/cheating. 3. In the family/neighbourhood – e.g. land and family properties. 4. Religious institutions/organizations -e.g. Diversion of resources. 5. In the office – Ministries/Departments/Agencies e.g. Bribery and corruption. 6. In the sharing of things/inheritance. 7. Port and harbours/Customs- e.g. clearing of goods/over and under-invoicing. 8. Educational institutions e.g. Examination malpractices/corruption. 9. Police/Immigration - e.g. extortion. 10. Social organisations —NGOs e.g. Corruption, etc.

questions.question:
SECTION B: THEMES FROM THE SYNOPTIC GOSPELS AND THE ACTS OF THE APOSTLES

 

(A) “Lord, how often shall my brother sin against me, and I forgive him?”

Recount Jesus’ response to the above question.
 
(B) State three lessons that can be learnt from Jesus’ teaching on forgiveness.
questions.explanation: (A) Jesus’ teaching on forgiveness (Matthew 18:21-35) Points expected of candidates are highlighted below; 1. Jesus told the story of the unmerciful servant in response to Peter’s question on how often one should show forgiveness to his/her neighbour. 2. Peter asked Jesus if it was seven times one should forgive one’s brother. 3. Jesus told him that one should forgive seventy times seven and not seven times. 4. To illustrate this, Jesus compared the Kingdom of heaven to a king who wished to settle accounts with his servants. 5. In the process, one of his debtors who owed him ten thousand talents was brought to him to settle his debt. 6. As he could not pay his debt, the king ordered that he, his wife, children and all that he had be sold to settle the debt. 7. The debtor then fell on his knees and pleaded with the king to be patient so that he would settle the debt later. 8. Out of pity, the king released the man and forgave him the debt. 9. Interestingly, the same man who was forgiven his debt went out and found his fellow servant who owed him only a hundred denarii. 10. He grabbed him by his throat and demanded instant payment. 11. His fellow servant fell on his knees and pleaded for payment to be made later. 12. But the man refused the request and put his fellow servant in prison until the debt was settled. 13. When his fellow servants saw’ what had happened, they became distressed and reported the case to the king. 14. The king summoned the man and rebuked him for not showing mercy to the fellow servant who owed him. 15. In anger, the King handed the man over to the jailers until he had settled all his debt. 16. Jesus concluded that it is the same way that God would do to every one of us if we do not forgive our brother from our hearts/God would not forgive anyone who failed to forgive others. (B) State three lessons that can be learnt from Jesus’ teaching on forgiveness. 1. It builds trust and confidence among people. 2. It is a sign of maturity. 3. It elicits repentance/remorsefulness and confession. 4. It leads to rehabilitation and reconciliation. 5. Facilitates prayers.

questions.question:
SECTION B: THEMES FROM THE SYNOPTIC GOSPELS AND THE ACTS OF THE APOSTLES

 
(A) Examine the trials of Jesus before Pilate as recorded in Luke’s Gospel.
 
(B) State three elements of a fair trial.
questions.explanation: (A) The trial of Jesus before Pilate as recorded by Luke’s gospel (Luke 23:1-12) 1. After Jesus had been found guilty of blasphemy for claiming to be the Christ a King, the Jewish Council brought him before Pilate. 2. The Sanhedrin had earlier passed the death sentence on him. 3. But the council had no legal right to execute the death sentence on Jesus without approval from the Romans. 4. The Sanhedrin was therefore required to send Jesus to Pontius Pilate, the Roman representative for trial. 5. And in order to make Jesus guilty before Pilate, they changed the charges levelled against him from religious blasphemy to political insurgence and revolution. 6. Jesus was accused of perverting the nation. 7. He was also charged with claiming to be a king. 8. Jesus was accused of forbidding the payment of taxes to Caesar. 9. Pilate asked Jesus if he was a King of the Jews, and Jesus answered in the affirmative. 10. Eventually, Pilate told the chief Priest and the crowd that Jesus was innocent by saying” I find no crime in this man”. 11. But the people said Jesus stirs up people, teaching throughout all Judea from Galilee. 12. When Pilate discovered that Jesus was a Galilean and belonged to Herod Antipas’ jurisdiction, he decided to send him to Herod Antipas. 13. After Herod had asked Jesus some questions at length and he did not answer, he mocked him and treated him with contempt. 14. Herod realised that Jesus was innocent even though his opponents accused him vehemently. 15. Finally, Herod returned Jesus to Pilate and on that day Pilate and Herod became friends as they were previously enemies. (B) Points expected of candidates are outlined below; 1. People should be given the right to public hearing. 2. People accused must have the right to counsel. 3. Judges in the courts must be impartial and not affected by conflict of interest. 4. People must have the right to appeal or a review of sentence. 5. People must have the right to be heard within a reasonable time. 6. An accused person should be deemed innocent until proven guilty. 7. Evidence should be sufficient and reliable/ no false witnesses. 8. There should be no interference in the work of the Judiciary/ independence of the Judiciary must be respected. 9. Judges must enjoy good conditions of service/ good pay /retire on their salary. 10. The Judiciary should be bold and fearless. 11. Citizens should ensure that justice is done at all times without fear or favour, to all manner of people. 12. Suspects should not be intimidated or tortured to elicit information.

questions.question:
SECTION B: THEMES FROM THE SYNOPTIC GOSPELS AND THE ACTS OF THE APOSTLES

 
(A) Highlight the persecution Peter and John had after the healing of the lame man.
 
(B) Mention two lessons that can be learnt from the reaction of Peter and John.
questions.explanation: (A) The persecution of Peter and John after the healing of the lame man. (Acts 4: 1-31) 1. After the healing of the cripple at the Beautiful Gate, the lame man demonstrated his cure by leaping and praising God, as he accompanied the disciples into the temple. 2. Many people recognized the cured man and they were amazed. 3. As they gathered, Peter and John preached and about 5,000 were converted. 4. Peter attributed their ability to heal the man at the Beautiful Gate to the resurrected Christ. 5. There was so much noise in the temple that Peter and John were arrested by the Priests, the Sadducees and the captain of the temple. 6. They were put in custody and tried by the council the following day. 7. During the trial, they were asked to tell the source of the power they used to heal the cripple. 8. Peter, filled with the Holy Spirit answered that it was through the name of Jesus Christ of Nazareth, whom they crucified but God raised from the dead. 9. Peter also said that apart from Jesus, there was no other name by which men would be saved. 10. Peter added that Jesus is the stone which the builders rejected but has become the cornerstone. 11. The Sanhedrin upon seeing the boldness of Peter and John and perceiving that they were uneducated, common men, realized that they had been with Jesus. 12. The Council saw the man who had been healed standing with them and they could not press any charge against them. 13. The captain of the temple and the Sadducees who did not believe in the resurrection were annoyed because the disciples were proclaiming Jesus’ resurrection from death. 14. Thus the Sanhedrin decided to restrain Peter and John by commanding them not to speak in the name of Jesus again. 15. But Peter and John resolutely insisted that they would obey God rather than man. 16. They were then set free and they joined the other apostles to pray, thanking God and asking for more boldness to speak the word of God and perform miracles. 17. As they prayed, the place where they stood shook and they were filled with the Holy Spirit. (B) Lessons that can be learnt from the reaction of Peter and John 1. We should be bold and resolute in doing God’s work/perseverance. 2. It is better to obey God than men/have faith in God. 3. Opposition and persecution can never stop God’s work. 4. It is only God who equips one for his work. 5. We should be willing to die for our beliefs. 6. We should pray and thank God in every situation. 7. We need to value our principles.

questions.question:
SECTION C: THEMES FROM SELECTED EPISTLES

 
(A) Explain James’ advice to Christians to be doers of the word and not hearers only.
 
(B) State two factors that hinder Christians from doing the will of God.
questions.explanation: (A) James’ advice to Christians to be doers of the word and not hearers only. (James 1:22-27, 2:14-26). Candidates are expected to list out points such as; 1. James advised Christians to live according to the word of the Lord, which they have heard. 2. He said it would be of no use to hear the word and fail to put it into practice. 3. According to James, if anyone is a hearer of the word and not a doer he is like someone who sees himself in a mirror and turns away and immediately forgets. 4. James says that, he who looks into the perfect law, and perseveres by doing it shall be blessed. 5. James is of the opinion that if one thinks he is religious but does not bridle his tongue, he deceives his heart and his religion is vain. 6. James holds the view that pure and undefiled religion before God entails visiting orphans and widows in their afflictions. 7. Pure religion also involves keeping oneself unstained from the world. 8. James says it is of no use to say you have faith but have no works to demonstrate the faith you have. 9. According to James, if someone is poorly clothed and hungry and you ask him to go in peace, and be warmed and filled without providing the clothing and food, then you are not backing your faith with works. 10. Hence, faith without works is dead/useless. 11. Abraham justified his faith by works when he was prepared to sacrifice his son, Isaac. 12. Abraham believed God and it was counted as righteousness and he was called a friend of God. 13. A person is therefore justified by works and not faith alone. 14. Similarly, Rahab the prostitute justified her faith by works when she received the messengers of Joshua and sent them out by another way.. 15. James concludes by saying that, as the body without the spirit is dead so also faith without works is dead. (B) Factors that hinder Christians from doing the will of God 1. Lack of faith/backsliding/unforgiving spirit 2. Unpleasant experiences 3. Desire to please the world/Materialism 4. Poverty 5. Fear 6. Lack of commitment/being ashamed to preach the word of God

questions.question:
SECTION C: THEMES FROM SELECTED EPISTLES

 

Peter’s teaching on interpersonal relationship among Christians. (1 Peter 5:1-11)
questions.explanation: Candidates are required to state that; 1. Peter exhorts elders of the church to tend the flock willingly and not by constraint. 2. The elders are to care for the flock, not for any gain but eagerly. 3. They are not to be domineering over those in their charge. 4. Instead, they are to set good examples for the flock to emulate. 5. Peter made the elders aware that when the chief shepherd appears, they will obtain the unfading crown of glory. 6. Peter also admonished the younger ones in the church to be subject to the elders. 7. According to Peter, Christians should clothe themselves with humility towards one another. 8. As God opposes the proud and gives grace to the humble. 9. Peter further advised the younger ones to humble themselves under God’s mighty hand. 10. And in due time, the Lord will exalt them. 11. Peter also advised Christians to cast all their anxieties on the Lord. 12. He asked Christians to resist the devil and he would flee from them. 13. Finally, they should stand firm in their faith for the enemy was always seeking an opportunity to attack them. 14. Peter encouraged Christians to endure suffering in such a way that the grace of God would be manifested in their lives. 15. He said that Christian suffering would last only for a while but the glory of Christ would be eternal.

questions.question:
SECTION A: THEMES FROM THE OLD TESTAMENT
 
(a) Highlight the story of how the Israelites crossed the Red Sea.
(b) State two lessons which Christians can learn from this incident
questions.explanation: HOW THE ISRAELITES CROSSED THE RED SEA. (EXODUS 14). i. After the ten plagues, Pharaoh allowed the Israelites to leave Egypt for the wilderness to worship their God. ii. Later, when Pharaoh realized that the Israelites had left for good, he regretted for allowing them to go. iii The Israelites were guarded by the Lord by a pillar of cloud during the day and pillar of fire by night. iv. Pharaoh quickly organized his soldiers and chariots to chase the Israelites with the hope of bringing them back. v. God allowed Pharaoh and his charioteers to pursue the Israelites in order to gain glory over the Egyptians. vi. They caught up with them at Pihahiroth where they had encamped in front of the sea. vii. When the Egyptians drew nearer, the Israelites became afraid and panicked/displaying lack of faith in God and Moses. vii. They cried to the Lord and began to accuse Moses for bringing them into the wilderness to die. ix. They said that they should have been left in Egypt to serve the Egyptians than to die in the wilderness. x. Moses told them not to entertain any fear but to stand firm for the Lord would fight for them. xi. Moses again said that in no time they would not see the Egyptians again. xii. Moses then cried to God and he was told by God to stretch his rod over the sea. xii. After that, a great wind Came and drove back the waters. xiv. The Israelites passed through on dry land/ground. xv. The Egyptians gave them a hot chase, but the wheels of their chariots could not move xvi. Moses immediately stretched his rod over the sea and the waters returned leading to the drowning of the Egyptians. xvii. The people then came to believe in Yahweh and in Moses His servant. B. LESSONS TO BE LEARNT FROM THE CROSSING OF THE RED SEA İ. Need to have faith in God. ii. God is always ready to protect his people in time of crisis/ provide a Way of escape for his people. iii. God will never allow our enemies to overcome us. iv. God is faithful and reliable/ always loyal to his people. V. Need to be patient in times of trouble/ crisis. vi. Need to pray always in difficult times vii. Need to seek God at all times/ being obedient to God's word/command. vii. We should have trust in our leaders. ix. Leaders must be Confident always and inspire their followers to have same. x. Leaders should encourage their followers always in time of difficulty to stand firm and not panic. xi. God punishes those who do not believe in Him/humbles them. xii. God is sovereign/Can do the impossible. xiii. Fear and panic weaken our faith and cause us to speak evil against God and spiritual leaders

questions.question:
SECTION A: THEMES FROM THE OLD TESTAMENT
 
(a) However, I will not tear away all the kingdom, but I will give one tribe to your son, for the sake David my servant.....Recount what led to the above pronouncement
questions.explanation: A. REASONS FOR THE PRONOUNCEMENT (1 KINGS 11:1-13) i. When Solomon had established himself as King of lsrael after his father David, he started loving many foreign women of whom God had warned him not to marry. ii. Those women included the daughter of Pharaoh and Moabite, Edomite, Sidonian and Hittite Women. iii. The reason was that they would surely turn away his heart after their gods. iv. Thus, during the latter part of Solomon's reign, his heart turned away from God who had appeared to him twice. V. This came about because he married many foreign wives against God's will. vi, He had seven hundred wives and three hundred concubines and these women-led him astray. vii. Solomon built high places for the gods of his foreign wives who burnt incense and sacrificed to their gods there, viii, He built high places for Chemosh, the abomination of Moab, Molech the abomination. of Ammon, ix, God was angry with Solomon because his heart had turned away from the God of Israel. x. His marriage of foreign wives also led to the adulteration of the worship of Yahweh. xi. God was not pleased with Solomon, because he did not follow Him wholeheartedly as his father, David did. xi. God, therefore, decided to divide the Davidic Kingdom of Israel into two after the death of Solomon. xiii. The Lord said to Solomon "Since this has been your mind and you have not kept my Covenant and status which l have commanded you, I will surely tear the Kíngdom from you and give it to your servant". xiv. One tribe (Judah) was to be retained for the sake of David and for the sake of Jerusalem which Yahweh had chosen. Xv. Solomon who had previously been devoted to God backslid from the worship of God/His wives turned away his heart after other gods. xvi. Solomon was however assured that for the sake of his father David, the prophecy would not happen during his days but during the days of his son.

questions.question:
SECTION A: THEMES FROM THE OLD TESTAMENT
 
(a) Outline Nehemiah's immediate reactions to the news about the state of affairs in Jerusalem
(b) Identify three virtues that can be learnt from Nehemiah's reactions
questions.explanation: A) HOW NEHEMIAH REACTED TO THE NEWS ABOUT THE STATE OF AFFAIRS IN JERUSALEM (NEHEMIAH 1:2-11) i. Nehemiah was one of the Jews taken into exile by Nebuchadnezzar ii. He was made a CUp-bearer to the king of Persia in Susa. iii. One day, Nehemiah was in Susa when a delegation led by his brother Hanani came to him with men from Judah. iv. Nehemiah asked them concerning the few Jews who were still in Jerusalem and about the city itself. v. Hanani made him aware that the people in Jerusalem were in great trouble and shame. vi. He further said that the walls of Jerusalem were broken down and its gates destroyed by fire. vii. Upon hearing that, Nehemiah broke down, wept, mourned and fasted for days. viii. Nehemiah prayed to God to hear the prayer of his servants ix. He confessed that He and his father's house had sinned. x. Again, he Confessed that they had not kept the commandments, statutes and ordinances Moses commanded. xi. He asked God to remember His words to Moses that if they were unfaithful he would scatter them among the people. xii. But should they repent and keep His commandment, He would gather them and restore them to the place He has chosen for them xiii. He reminded God that He had redeemed His people by His great power. xiv. He finally petitioned God to listen to His servant and grant him success and mercy. xv. After the prayer, God intervened and touched the heart of the king to grant him mercy, to visit his people. B. VIRTUES THAT CAN BE LEARNT FROM NEHEMIAH'S REACTION i. Nehemiah was patriotic; hence, we need to learn to show patriotism/ love our nation. ii. He was very prayerful. We need to emulate Nehemiah and be prayerful. iii. He was conscious of the sins Committed by him and his fellow Jews; so he confessed to God/ There is the need for a country to accept her sins and confession. iV. There is the need for national repentance. V. It is important to have faith in God/God is faithful. vi. We should always intercede for our nation/ pray for the well-being of our country. vii. There is the need to be focused/ committed. vii. We should have vision and share it with others. ix. We should be sincere to God by confessing our sins. x. We should show empathy with the plight of our people/selfless. xi. We should demonstrate humility and sincere service.

questions.question:
a) Give an account of Amos' encounter with Amaziah the priest
 
b) Indicate any three practices in your society that need to be condemned
questions.explanation: (A) AMOS ENCOUNTER WITH AMAZIAH THE PRIEST (AMOS 7:10-17) i. Amos was a shepherd and also a dresser of sycamore trees, while Amaziah was a priest at Bethel, the centre of Israel's apostate religion. ii. Amos denounced the social and religious malpractices of the Israelites of his day. iii. He also preached at the king's sanctuary that Jeroboam II would die by the sword. iv. This statement infuriated Amaziah the priest in-charge of the temple at Bethel. v. Amaziah reported Amos to the king, accusing him of treason. vi. Since the temple belonged to the king and not God Amos was forbidden to speak against the king there. vii. Amaziah commanded Amos to return to Judah to prophesy and earn his living there. viii. tie called Amos a "seer" a prophet that was consulted for the discovery of lost articles for a fee. ix. Amos denied being a paid prophet lathe service of the king nor was he a member of the professional prophets. x. He said no one had engaged him to pronounce judgment on Jeroboam and Israel. xi. He was only a herdsman and a dresser of sycamore trees, and the Lord took him from following the flock in order to prophesy to Israel. xii. According to Amos, no authority could stop him from delivering his message. xiii. Amos then cursed Amaziah for trying to turn him away from God's command. xiv. He indicated that Amaziah's wife would be a prostitute and his children killed. xv. Furthermore, Amaziah's. land and property, would be divided among the people. xvi. Israel would go into exile. xvii. Finally, Amaziah would die in a foreign land. (B) Three Practices that Need to be Condemned i. Fake/Superficial worship and sacrifice! Occultism/Ancestral practices. ii. Ethnicity! Corruption! Injustice! Bribery Partiality. iii. Disrespect of the Sabbath/vows/False swearing. iv. Commercial preachers in vehicles and churches/Market places. v. Poor environment practices. vi. Festal virgins/Confinement of females to shrines. vii. Widowhood rites. viii. Display of wealth during harvest. ix. Female genital mutilation (FGM). x. Oppression of the poor/ uncaring attitude/ child abuse. xi. Sexual immorality/Homosexuality.

questions.question:
(a) Examine the baptism of Jesus as narrated in Matthew's Gospel
 
(b) In what two ways is baptism relevant to Christian?
questions.explanation: A) THE BAPTISM OF JESUS (MATTHEW 3:13-17) i. When Jesus heard of the work of John the Baptist, he came down from Galilee to be baptized in the river Jordan. ii, John was preaching baptism for the forgiveness of sins. iii. When John saw Jesus he recognized Him as the expected Messiah - a man superior to him, iv. "It is I who need to be baptized by you, and are you coming to me?" said John. v. John therefore became hesitant in baptizing Jesus. vi, Jesus however persuaded John to baptize Turn in order to fulfill righteousness. vii. Based on this conviction, John consented to baptize Jesus through immersion. viii. As He came out of the water, the heavens opened and the spirit of the Lord descended and alighted on Him like a dove. ix, Immediately, a voice came from heaven saying, "This is my beloved son, with whom am well pleased". x. The baptism prepared Jesus for His earthly ministry as it marked His call into public office. xi. The descent of the spirit on Jesus was a symbol of Him being anointed as son of God/ being confirmed as the Messiah. xii. . Jesus underwent baptism in order to identify with sinners whom He came to redeem. xiii. The Holy Spirit which came upon Jesus led and guided Him to do God's will. xiv. By going to John for baptism, Jesus was giving approval to John's baptism of repentance for the forgiveness of sins. xv. Baptism therefore is a divine ritual necessary to fulfill all righteousness. B) Relevance of Baptism i. It marks membership to the Christian community/Identification with Christ and all Christians. ii. It is a response to God's command. iii. It is a symbol of the death and resurrection with Christ. iv. It is a sign of repentance and forgiveness. v. It marks a new beginning/creation/new life. vi. It marks the physical and ritual cleansing of Christians.

questions.question:
a) Describe the appearance of the Risen Christ to the two men on their way to Emmaus
 
(b) What three benefits to Christians derive from the resurrection of Jesus Christ?
questions.explanation: A) APPEARANCE OF JESUS TO THE MEN GOING TO (LUKE 24:13-35) i. On the first day of the week/ the evening of the resurrection, Cleopas and one other disciple were going to Emmaus discussing the most current event in Jerusalem, i.e the death and resurrection of Jesus Christ ii. Jesus drew near and walked with them, and joined the conversation iii. They could not recognize him and were surprised when he asked them what they were discussing iv. They asked him whether he was the only stranger around, unaware of the most current happening. v. He asked them what it was. They answered, it concerned Jesus. a great prophet that was mighty in words and deeds; vi And how the Jewish council had delivered him to be condemned to death vii, He was the one they had hoped would redeem Israel. viii. It was then the third day since it happened - though some of their women had amazed them with the story of his resurrection. ix. Some of their men had however been to the tomb and found it empty as the women had told them/but Jesus they did not see. x. Jesus called them fools who were slow of heart to believe all that the. prophets had spoken. xi. He said that, it was necessary that Christ should suffer and enter into glory. xii. Beginning with Moses and the prophets, he interpreted to them all that the scriptures had spoken about himself. xiii. When they drew near the village, Jesus made as though he would go further they pleaded with him to pass the night with them (for the day was spent). xiv. He went in with them and, at table; he took the bread, blessed and broke it. xv. And their eyes were Opened and they recognized that it was Jesus. xvi. Jesus disappeared from their sight. xvii. ' They wondered how it did not dawn on them, when he was expounding the scriptures to them, that they were actually talking to Jesus; xviii. They immediately returned to Jerusalem, told their experiences and the brethren in turn confirmed Jesus' resurrection. B) THREE BENEFITS CHRISTIANS DERIVE FROM THE RESURRECTION i. It is the main pillar of the Christian faith. ii. It gives Christians hope that Jesus is alive. iii. It confirms that Jesus is the son of God, iv. It shows that all those who die the Lord will be alive in the last day v. It confirms Christians hope for salvation. vi. ft gives Christians the boldness and courage to evangelize. vii. Jesus overcome death, so would Christians overcome death and the sorrow and pain it brings.

questions.question:
(a) Describe how Saul became converted
 
(b) Identify any three visible signs of a convert.
questions.explanation: (A) THE CONVERSION OF SAUL (ACTS 9:1-22) . i. Saul, after the persecution of the disciples in Jerusalem, collected letters from the high priest to the synagogue at Damascu ii. His intention was to arrest Christians and send them to Jerusalem for persecution. iii. As he approached Damascus, a light from heaven flashed about him iv. He fell down and heard a voice saying, "Saul, Saul why do you persecute me"? v. Upon enquiry, he found it was Jesus he was persecuting vi. He was asked to get up, go to the city and wait for farther instructions vii. The men with Saul stood speechless, hearing the voice but seeing no one. viii. Saul rose from the ground but could see nothing. ix. He was led to Damascus without his sight and for three days be neither ate nor drank. x. Ananias, a disciple at Damascus, was asked to go to the street called Straight and ask for Saul of Tarsus who was waiting to be healed. xi. Ananias was unwilling to go because he had heard the havoc Saul had done to the saints at Jerusalem. xii. God told Ananias to go and heal him because Saw was His chosen instrument to carry God's name to Gentiles and Kings. xiii. Ananias vent and laid his hands on him saying, "Brother Saul, the Lord Jesus who appeared to you on the way has sent me that you may regain your sight and be tilled with the Holy Spirit". xiv. Paul regained his sight (something like scales fell off his eyes). xv. He was baptized, took food and was strengthened. xvi. At Damascus he proclaimed in their synagogues that Jesus is the Son of God. B) THREE VISIBLE SIGNS OF A CONVERT i. Daily study of the word of God. ii. Embarking on evangelism/Fearless and bold to-spread the word of God. iii. Daily attendance at church services. iv. Commitment to the work of God/Faithfulness to God. v. Honesty in dealing with people/ Truthfulness, in daily life. vi. Transformed life/new person/upright life . vii. Ready to suffer for the Lord. viii. Participating in extra-church activities. ix. Helping to fight evil in the society.

questions.question:
(a) Highlight the relationship between faith and works according to the teaching of James
 
(b) In what three ways can Chris-tians demonstrate their faith in works?
questions.explanation: (A) RELATIONSHIP BETWEEN FAITH AND WORKS (JAMES 1:2-27,2: 14 - 26) i. James outlined the fact that a person gains no profit by merely claiming to have faith but not works. ii. Genuine faith is evidenced by works. He called on Christians to be doers of the word and not deceive themselves as men of faith, by not doing what they professed. iii. Thus faith without works is dead. iv. Faith is expressed in practical works like charity/caring for the sick, widows, v. Faith and works are inseparable for, you cannot show me your faith with, vi A person is justified by works and not by faith alone For works is the finality of it vii. James taught that people who have belief in God without expressing it in actions justify their faith are not different from the devil,. viii For the devil also believes in God but does not do God's work ix. James argued that if Christians are mere hearers, they are like a man who observe his face in a mirror, but as soon as he goes away, forgets what his face looks like. x. For somebody to be truly 'religious he must bridle his tongue, or else his religion is in vain! he is deceiving himself. xi. James argues further that Abraham was justified by works when he was ready to offer his son Isaac. Thus he justified his faith by works. xii. Again, Rahab the harlot was also justified by her works when she protected the spies sent by Joshua. She had faith in God and matched it by saving the spies. xiii. These two people expressed their faiths by their deeds. xiv. Faith and works are essential to each other just as the body arid the spirit. xv. Thus, just as the body apart from the spirit is dead, faith apart from works is dead. B) EXPRESSION OF FAITH IN WORKS. i Respecting themselves service to the society/country/charity. ii. Loving one another / being hospitable. iii. Being law abiding. iv. Performing one's civic responsibilities and religious obligations. v. Avoiding pride/arrogance and violence etc. vi, Being patient, submissive, polite, honest/practicing Christian virtues. vii. Ensuring good governance viii. Taking part in church activities.

questions.question:
SECTION A: THEMES FROM THE OLD TESTAMENT
 
(a) l am no prophet, nor a prophet's son, but I am a herdsman and a dresser of sycamore trees...give an account of the events that led to this statement.
(b) ldentify three reasons for which people complain about the activities of some men of God today.
questions.explanation: A. AMOS' ENCOUNTER WITH AMAZIAH (AMOS 7:10-17) i. Amos was a shepherd in Judah whom God called to prophesy in Israel. ii. He spoke against the social and religious malpractices of the Israelites of his day. iii. Amaziah, the priest at Bethel, reported Amos to the king of Israel, Jeroboam l, accusing him of conspiracy and treason. iv. According to Amaziah, Amos had prophesied that the king of Israel would go into exile. v. Amaziah then met Amos who had told him that he was forbidden to speak against the king and the temple. vi, Amaziah misconstrued Amos for one of the many false prophets of the time and called him a seer (a professional prophet who prophesies for a living). vi. Amaziah commanded Amos to return to Judah, his home town to prophesy and earn a living there and never again at Bethel. vii. This was because Bethel was the King's sanctuary and the temple of the kingdom. ix. Amos disassociated himself from the wrong impression created about him by Amaziah. x. He told Amaziah that the Lord called him to prophesy in Israel while he was tending his flock and dressing the sycamore trees. xi. And for challenging him, Amos told Amaziah that his wife would become a harlot in the city and his sons shall fall by the sword and he Amaziah would die in exile. B.WHY PEOPLE COMPLAIN ABOUT THE ACTIVITIES OF SOME MEN OF GOD i. Use of occultic/magical powers. ii. Commercialisation of the gospel/extortion. iii. Discrimination against the p0or and underprivileged. iv. Immorality/ immoral lives. v. False doctrines. vi. False prophecies/ not trustworthy. vii. Lack of adequate education. vii. Embezzlement/ misappropriation of funds. ix. Over-emphasis on prosperity messages above salvation and redemption. x. Political alignment. xi. Display of wealth and opulence. xi. Mismanagement of church resources. xii. Abuse of power and position.

questions.question:
THEMES FROM THE SYNOPTIC GOSPELS AND THE ACTS OF THE APOSTLES

'
(a) Relate the trial of Jesus before the Sanhedrin according to Mark's gospel.
(b) Give two reasons for which people bear false witness against others.
questions.explanation: A. THE TRIAL OF JESUS BEFORE THE ŠANHEDRIN ACCORDING TO MARK (MARK 14:53-65) i. After Jesus was arrested in the garden of Gethsemane, Peter followed at a distance into the courtyard of the high priest and there warmed himself at the fire. ii. The Sanhedrin sought false testimony against Jesus to put him to death but they found none. iii. The Sanhedrin was a body of religious leaders presided by the high priest. iv. Many people came to give false evidence against him but their statements did not tally. v. But finally, in accordance 1lse with Jewish law, two witnesses came forward and accused Jesus of saying that he would destroy the temple Jon in Jerusalem and in three days build another. vi. The temple stood as the centre of Judaism; thus, Jesus was attacking the heart of the Jewish religion. vii. The high priest then asked Jesus under oath whether he was the Messiah, the son of the Blessed One. vii. Jesus replied affirmatively that he was the Messiah. ix. He also said that they would see the Son of Man seated at the right hand of power and coming with the clouds of heaven. x. The high priest then tore his garment as a sign of righteous indignation and asked if they needed a further evidence against this blasphemy. xi. According to the high priest, Jesus had spoken blasphemy, so, he sought to the decision of the council. xii. The whole council condemned Jesus and said that he deserved death as a ber penalty for blasphemy. xiii. Eventually, some members of the Sanhedrin spat on him, while others covered his face and struck him to express their contempt and hate for his Messianic claims. xiv. They asked Jesus to prophesy and mention the one who struck him. xv. The guards likewise gave him some blows B. REASONS WHY PEOPLE BEAR FALSE WITNESS AGAINST OTHERS İ. Hatred/character assassination/ defamation ii. Envy/ jealousy iii. Greed iv. Vengeance/ retribution v. Bribery/monetary gains vi. To win favour vi. Religious/tribal /filial reasons vii. Coercion/ force ix. Out of fear x. For selfish interest xi. To incriminate eliminate

questions.question:
THEMES FROM THE SYNOPTIC GOSPELS AND THE ACTS OF THE APOSTLES

(a) My soul is very sorrowful, even to death; remain here and watch with me. Give an account of what happened to Jesus after he made this statement.
(b) identify two ways by which one can assist a fellow Christian going through challenges
questions.explanation: A. JESUS' AGONY AND ARREST IN THE GARDEN OF GETHSEMANE (MATTHEW 26:36-56) i. Jesus and his disciples went to the garden of Gethsemane to pray. ii. He took with him Peter, James and John (member of his inner circle) to another place, leaving the rest behind. iii. Jesus then left the three and went further to pray alone. iv. He became greatly distressed and made the above statement. v. He then went a little farther on and fell tọ the ground to pray, saying my father if it be possible, let this cup pass from me; neverthless God's will should be done vi. This prayer shows the profound humanity of Jesus and his resolute courage and submission to the will of God. vii. The cup in this context is a symbol or deep sorrow and suffering. viii. Jesus came back to the three, Peter, James and John found them sleeping and he asked Peter whether they could not watch with him for one hour. ix. Jesus then told them to watch and pray so that they would not enter into temptation. x. He said the spirit is willing but the body is weak. xi. This means that though the disciples had the best of intentions, the weakness of the flesh failed them. xii. Again, for the second time, Jesus went away to pray and he again asked that if it was possible the cup should pass by him. xii. Jesus came back and found the three disciples asleep again xiv. Jesus left them and went to pray for the third time and he came back to meet the disciples still asleep. xv. He asked them whether they were still sleeping and taking their rest. Xvi. Jesus then told them that the hour was at hand and the Son of Man would be betrayed into the hands of sinners. xvi. He made them aware that the betrayer was at hand so they should get ready to go. xvii. As Jesus was speaking,. Judas Iscariot led a crowd with swords and clubs to arrest him. xix. But one of these who stood by drew his sword and cut the ear of the high priest's slave but Jesus restrained him. xx. The crowd then arrested Jesus after Judas had kissed him. xxi. They led Him to the high priest's house, for the Jewish trial. B. WAYS BY WHICH ONE GOING THROUGH CHALLENGES CAN BE ASSISTED i. Visiting the one going through the challenges. ii. Praying with the person having the problem. iii. Assisting the person in cash or in-kind when necessary/ sharing your resources with him or her. iv. Counselling the victim/ providing advice. v. Relocating the victim/ changing victim's environment. vi. Seeking redress/justice. vii. Speaking on their behalf advocacy. vii. Encouraging the person to trust in God. ix. Show love/empathy.

questions.question:
THEMES FROM THE SYNOPTIC GOSPELS AND THE ACTS OF THE APOSTLES
 
(a) Give an account of Stephen's defence before the Sanhedrin.
(b) State three lessons that can be learnt from Stephen's defence.
questions.explanation: STEPHEN'S DEFENCĚ BEFORE THE SANHEDRIN (ACT6: 2-6; 8-9 7:1-10) i. Stephen was one of the seven deacons appointed to be in charge of the welfare of the poor and needy in the early church. ii. He was full of faith, grace and power and performed great wonders and signs among the people. iii. Some of the Jews argued with Stephen but they could not withstand the wisdom and the spirit with which he spoke. iv. They instigated some men who accused Stephen of speaking blasphemous words against God and Moses. v Specifically, that Jesus of Nazareth would destroy the temple, and change the customs which Moses delivered to them. vi. By Jewish law, the accusations leveled against Stephen constituted serious offence punishable by death. vii. In his defence, Stephen tried to prove that even in the past, God did not confine His presence to the temple at Jerusalem. viii. He decided to trace the history of the Jews to show that God is universal and does not only dwell in the temple. ix. He cited the example of how God appeared to Abraham when he was in Mesopotamia and asked him to go and live in Haran and Abraham obeyed. x. He stressed that God told Abraham that his descendants would become slaves in another country where they would be maltreated for four hundred years xi. But God would punish that nation which enslaved them and later Abraham's decendants would go out and Worship him in the land of Canaan. Xii. Again, Stephen said that God gave Abraham the covenant of circumcision and when he became the father of Isaac, he circumcised him on the eighth day. xii. Isaac also became the father of Jacob and Jacob became the father of the patriarchs. xiv. The Patriarchs were jealous of Jacob and sold him into Egypt. xv. God was with Joseph and rescued him from all afflictions. B.LESSONS TÖ BE LEARNT FROM STEPHEN'S DEFENCE I. We should be bold and courageous when we face trials. ii. We should have strong faith in God. iii. In times of persecution, we should rely on God to defend us iv When God blesses us, the enemy cannot overcome us v There is the need to remember our history vi bearing false witness destroys one's personality/ integrity vii To obtain protection against the devil. we should always pray. viii. We should be prepared to defend our faith even when we face opposition ix We should forgive those who hurt us. x. We should be bold to spread the gospel. xi We should be knowledgeable in scriptures. xii. We should be respectful to elders.

questions.question:
SECTION C: THEMES FROM SELECTED EPISTLES
(a) Therefore confess your sins to one another, and pray for one another, that you may be healed... What other teachings did James give on effective prayer?
(b) In what three ways are Christians misusing prayers today?
questions.explanation: A. JAMES' TEACHING ON EFFECTIVE PRAYER(JAMES 1:2-8; 5:13-18) i To James, effective prayer is one that God answers. ii. And to achieve this, one needs to repent and confess one's sins to God and to one another in order to attract God's healing and forgiveness of sin, iii James encouraged Christians to count it all joy whenever they meet trials. iv. He says when one's faith is tested through trials, one becomes steadfast and later becomes perfect and complete. v. According to James, if anyone lacks wisdom, he should ask God in prayer and he would have it generously. vi. James holds the view that one must pray in faith without doubting Vil. For anyone who doubts is like a wave of the sea that is driven and tossed by the wind. vii. And that, a person who doubts will receive nothing from the Lord. ix. He again said that if anyone is indisposed, he should call upon the elders of the church to anoint him with oil and pray in humility,. x. And that, the prayer of faith will heal the sick. xi. James revealed that God is glorified when people pray for the right things. xii. Thus, prayer should be made according to the will of God. xii. James urged Christians to pray in humility. XiV. Christians should be persistent in prayer by praying unceasingly till their requests are met xv. James is of the opinion that the fervent prayer of the righteous has a great effect xvi. He gave an example of Elijah who prayed fervently for no rain and there was no rain for three and half years. Xvii. And after three and half years, he prayed again and there was rain B. HOW PRAYERS ARE MISUSED BY CHRISTIANS TODAY İ Paying money for prayers/ consultation fee for prayers/ Commercialisation of prayers. ii. Cursing people in prayers/ praying against enemies. iii Praying at the wrong time when they should be working/substituting prayer for work. iv. Shouting making noise to disturb others. v. Prayers for the highest donor/ bidders. vi. Substituting prayers for righteousness. vii. Praying with selfish motives. viii. Praying not in accordance with the word/will of God. ix. idolatry in prayer/praying to religious leaders rather than God. X. Effectiveness of prayer wrongly associated with material objects, e.g. salt candle, stickers, anointing oil, etc.

questions.question:
SECTION C: THEMES FROM SELECTED EPISTLES
 
(a) Highlight the attitude Peter recommended for Christians living among people of other faiths.
(b) State two factors that can make Christians turn away from pleasing God.
questions.explanation: A. ATTITUDE PETER RECOMMENDED FOR CHRISTIANS LIVING AMONG PEOPLE OF OTHER FAITHS (1 PETER 2: 1-25). i. Peter advised Christians to put away all malice, deceit, hypocrisy, envy, and slander ii He said Christians should long for the pure spiritual milk (the word of God) so that they may grow up unto salvation iii. Peter referred to Christians as a chosen race, a royal priesthood, a holy nation. iv He further said that they are a people for His own possession who have been called out of darkness into His marvelous light. v According to Peter, Christians were formerly not a people but now they are God's people, /hitherto they had not received mercy but now they have received mercy vi, Peter urged Christians that, as sojourners and exiles, they should abstain from the passions of the flesh which wage war against the soul (E.g. Drunkenness/ lawlessness/idolatry vii Peter said Christians should do good deeds among Gentiles so that they may see their good deeds and give glory to God/maintain good conduct viii. In his letter, Peter advised Christians to be loyal to their masters whether they are gentle or oppressive / Be subjected to every human institution. ix, He said Christians should do good so as to silence the ignorance of foolish men. x. Again, Christians should live as free people of God but they should not use their freedom as cover-up for evil xi. According to Peter, Christians should live as servants of God and should honor everyone xii Christians should also love the brotherhood, fear God, and honor the emperor xiii. Peter says a servant Is approved of his calling if he endured pain while suffering oppression xiv According to Peter, it is unacceptable if a servant is beaten for his wrong deed and he retaliates xv But when one does evil and suffers for it, yet bears it patiently, he wins God's approval. Xvi. Peter finally said that Jesus is a good example of the suffering servant who should be emulated B, FACTORS THAT CAN MAKE CHRISTIANS TURN AWAY FROM PLEASING GOD i Desires of the flesh/greed. li, False doctrines. iii Harsh economic conditions iv. Ignorance of the word of God. v. Persecutions/ fear of men. vi. Difficult bitter or unpleasant experiences/ situations. vii Materialism vii. Cultural traditional practices viii Unforgiving spirit. ix. Lack of faith. x. Disappointments thinking God is not listening. xi, Occultic practices xii Discrimination / Favouritism

questions.question:
(a) Highlight the steps taken by God to change a formless earth to a place of life and activity

(b) ldentify four ways human beings are destroying God's creation.
questions.explanation: A. How God changed a formless earth to a place of life and activity (Genesis 1:1-31): i. In the beginning, God created the heavens and the earth. ii. The earth was formless, and the spirit of God hovered on the face of the waters. iii. God commanded the light to appear on the formless, empty, and dark earth. iv. He then separated the light from the darkness and called the light day and the darkness níght. v. Again, God made the expanse and separated the waters under the expanse from the water above and called it sky. vi. The water below the expanse was then gathered to one place to create dry ground. vii. The dry ground God called land and the gathered water, seas. viii. God then caused the land to produce vegetation of plants bearing seeds according to their kind and trees bearing fruits. ix. Further, God created the seasons, days and years, and lights in the expanse of the sky to give light on the earth. x. God made two great lights- the greater light to govern the day and the lesser light to govern the night. xi. This was followed by the creation of the great creatures of the sea and every living and moving thing. xii. Every winged bird according to its kind was also created to fly across the expanse of the sky. xiii. The creatures of the sea and the birds were commanded to increase in number to fill the water in the sea and the earth respectively. xiv. Liveştock, creatures that move along the ground, and wild animals were also created. xv. God then created man in His own image and likeness to rule over the fish of the sea and the birds of the air and all creatures. xvi. God blessed the man and woman to be fruitful and increase in number to fill the earth and subdue it. B Ways humans are destroying God's creation: i. legal mining/galamsey/sand mining. ii Overgrazing. iii Pollution -water, air, and noise. iv. Indiscriminate waste disposal. v. Over-exploitation of natural resources/ deforestation/overfishing/overhunting. vi. Genetic engineering (cloning). vi. Homosexuality/lesbianism.

questions.question:
(a) State the instructions God gave to Joshua on Joshua's assumption of leadership over Israel.

(b) Briefly explain the various lessons political leaders can learn from Joshua's experience.
questions.explanation: A. God's instructions to Joshua on his assumption of leadership over lsrael (Numbers 27:15-23;Joshua 1:1-9): . i When Moses was about to exit the leadership position of lsrael, he prayed to God to appoint his Successor in order not to leave the people like sheep without a shepherd. ii, So, the Lord ordered Moses to take Joshua, the son of Nun, a man in whom is the spirit and lay hand on him. iii. Joshua was to be brought before Eleazar the priest and the entire assembly to be commissioned. iv. Moses did as was commanded by the Lord and Joshua was brought before Eleazar the priest and the whole assembly who commissioned and laid hand on him. V. God then promised to give Joshua every place that the sole of his feet would tread. vi. The territory extending from the desert to Lebanon and from the great river, Euphrates to the Great Sea. vi. The Lord promised to be with Joshua as He was with Moses. vii. And no one would be able to stand against him all the days of his life. ix. Joshua was to be strong and courageous as he would lead the Israelites to inherit the land promised their forefathers. x. He was to be careful to obey all the law Moses gave him to be successful wherever he went. xi. Joshua was to make sure the book of the law never departed from his mouth but to meditate upon it day and night. xii. He was to apply the law in everything to be prosperous and successful xiii. Joshua was to be courageous and strong and not to be terrified or discouraged, for the Lord would be with him wherever he went. B Lessons political leaders can learn from Joshua's experience: 1. Political leaders should not impose successors but allow God to lead in making such a choice ii. They should help the people to elect leaders who are goal-oriented and people-oriented iii Political leaders should know when enough is enough and retire honourably iv. They should be interested in grooming people who can take over from them. v Like Moses, they should show confidence in the authority and abilities of their successors to rule vi. They must be confident that they can only succeed when they observe God's prescriptions vii Political leaders should be patient as they wait to assume leadership positions and not take power through evil manipulations or by force of arms viii Political leaders should be courageous and obedient in all they do

questions.question:
(a) State the different ways David resisted taking Saul's life at the wilderness of Ziph.

(b) Mention four benefits one can derive from self-control.
questions.explanation: A How David resisted taking Saul's life at the wilderness of Ziph (1 Samuel 26:1-25): i Saul received a report from the Ziphites that David was hiding on the hill of Hachilah ii So, Saul went in search of David at the Desert of Ziph with three thousand chosen men iii Saul and his men made their camp beside the road on the hill of Hachilah facing Jeshimon whilst David stayed in the desert iv. When David heard of the presence of Saul, he sent men to scout the whereabouts of Saul and this was confirmed. v. With this information. David and Abishai went to the camp of Saul and saw him and Abner, the commander of the army lying down sleeping with the army encamped around them vi. Abishai said to David that the Lord had delivered his enemy into head and that David should allow him to kill Saul. vii. David rebuked Abishai because it is a sin to kill the lords anointed. viii. David again said that Saul should be allowed to die in the hands of the Lord or in battle but not in his hand / the life of Saul was in God's hands. ix., David then ordered Sauľ's spear that was stuck to the ground near his head and his water jar to be taken away x. When David crossed to the other side, he called to Saul and his men saying they had failed to protect the King and that Abner, the Army Commander deserved to die Xi. Saul then called out to David and he responded by asking why Saul was pursuing him and what his guilt was. xii. David, however, said if it was the Lord's doing; then He should accept an offering but if it were men. they must be cursed before the Lord. xiii. David wondered why the king of Israel should be hunting him like a partridge in the mountain. xiv. Saul apologized to David and promised not to harm him because he had spared his life. xV. David handed over Saul's spear and water jug to him and noted that the Lord rewards everyone for his/her righteousness and faithfulness. xvi. David ended by saying that the Lord had delivered Saul into his hand but he would not lay hands on the Lord's anointed. xvii. Because I valued your life, may the Lord value my life and deliver me from all troubles. xviii, Saul blessed David and they both departed. B. Benefits of self-control: i. It is a sign of maturity/principled. ii. it fosters harmonious living with others. iii. It prevents reckless talks and actions/avoidance of temptation. iv. It ensures well-thought out decisions. v. It accords oneself respect and respect for others. vi. It ensures peaceful resolution of disputes. vii. It prevents tension/conflict/war. viii. It builds trust/confidence. ix. It promotes good health/healthy life.

questions.question:
(a) Give an account of Solomon's prayer during the dediçation of the temple.

(b) Explain three ways leaders can use their resources for the development of the society.
questions.explanation: A. Solomon's prayer at the dedication of the temple (1 Kings 8: 1-53): i After the completion of the Temple, Solomon assembled all the elders and chiefs of lsrael for the dedication of the Temple. ii. He had the ark of the Lord brought from Zion and placed beneath the wings of the cherubim situated at the Most Holy place of the Temple. iii. Standing before the altar of the Lord in front of the Assembly with hands spread towards heaven, Solomon acknowledged the supremacy of God and His faithfulness to His promise to David. iv. Solomon urged the Lord to keep the promise made to David that there would always be a man to sit before Him on the throne if only his children would be obedient to the Lord, v. Solomon acknowledged that like the earth and heaven, the Temple could not contain the Lord. vi. He, however, appealed to the Lord to have mercy and hear his cry and prayer in His presence. vii. Solomon requested of the Lord to open His eyes towards the Temple day and night so that He would hear the prayer of His servants towards this place. viii. When a man wrongs his neighbor and is required to take an oath before your altar in this Temple, hear from heaven and act ix. Judge between servants, condemning the guilty and bringing down on his own head what he has done/declare the innocent not guilty, and so establish his innocence. x. When Israel is defeated at war due to sin against you but they confess to your name in the Temple, bring them again to the land of their forefathers, xi. If there is drought or famine due to sins of your people and they turn to you in supplication in the Temple, give them rain. xii. In times of disaster or disease, when the people pray with hands towards the Temple, forgive and deliver them. xiii. When a foreigner hears of your name and comes to pray towards the Temple, grant his request so that all the people of the earth would know you. xiv. Let Israel win all its wars when they pray towards your city and the Temple that i have built for your name. xv Even when Israel is taken into captivity due to your anger and they repent and pray towards your chosen city and the Temple, hear their prayers and uphold their cause. B. Ways leaders can use resources for the development of society: i. Provision of social amenities. ii. Investing in the marginalized society. iii, Avoiding corruption/mismanagement. iv. Equitable distribution of resources. v. Education and training for all persons. vi. Avoiding unnecessary litigation and wars/conflict. Vii. Investing in projects that take into consideration generations yet unborn. viii. Protection of women's and children's rights. ix. Ensuring religious freedom.

questions.question:
(a) Discuss the circumstances that led to Jesus saying "Do not be afraid; henceforth you will be catching men

(b) Enumerate three factors that prevent people from becoming committed Christians.
questions.explanation: A "Do not be afraid: henceforth you will be catching men" The Circumstance that led to the statement (Luke 5:1-11: İ. Jesus stood by the lake Gennesaret and the people gathered to hear the word of God from him. ii. Jesus saw two empty boats and entered one of them belonging to Simon Peter. iii Jesus stood in the boat and taught the people around. iv. After the teaching, Jesus instructed Peter to cast his nets in the deep waters for a catch. v. Simon initially protested but later agreed to do as Jesus directed. vi. After he threw the nets, he caught a great shoal of fish. vi. His nets were breaking, and he had to request assistance from his colleagues. vii. They filled the two boats so that they began to sink. viii. Peter was so much astonished that he begged Jesus to depart from him since he was a sinner. ix. Peter was in the company of James and John, the Sons of Zebedee who were also fishermen. x. Jesus then invited them to be fishers of men. xi. And instantly, they left everything and followed Jesus. B. Factors that prevent people from becoming committed Christians: i. Lack of self-denial. ii. Poverty iii. Lack of self-control. iv. Unforgiveness/intolerance. v. Unwilling to give up sinful habits/pride. vi. Wealth materialism. vii. Not praying regularly. viii. Not reading the Bible regularly. ix. Failure to abide by the word of God/lack of faith. x. Peer pressure/Bad company. xi.idolatry. xii. Demonic/satanic influence.

questions.question:
(a) Give an account of the burial of Jesus as narrated by the Synoptic Gospels.

(b) Mention three ways money is overspent during funerals in society.
questions.explanation: The burial of Jesus as narrated by the Synoptic Gospels (Matthew 27:57-66: Mark 15:42-47: Luke 23:50-56): i. Jesus was condemned to death by the Sanhedrin and Pilate. ii. Jesus was crucified between two robbers at Golgotha. iii. He was crucified on the preparation day, that is, the day before the Sabbath. iv. Joseph of Arimathea, a rich/good and righteous man, was opposed to the Sanhedrin's condemnation of Jesus. v. On the evening of the crucifixion, Joseph of Arimathea, a member of the Sanhedrin, went to Pilate and asked for the body of Jesus. vi. Pilate granted the request of Joseph and gave the boby to him. vii. Joseph wrapped the body in a linen shroud. viii. The body was then laid in a new rock hewed tomb belonging to Joseph. ix A stone was was then rolled against the door of the tomb. x. The chief priest and Pharisees requested Pilate to deploy guards to secure the tomb of Jesus. xi. According to them, Jesus had claimed to rise from the grave after three days. xii. The women returned to prepare spices and ointments to anoint Jesus' body. xiii. Mary Magdalene, Mary the mother of James, and some other women from Galilee were at the tomb to see where Jesus was laid. xiv. According to Matthew's account, Pilate ordered that guards should be sent to secure the tomb. xv. AIl this was based on the fact that it was alleged that the disciples intended to go and steal Jesus' body. B. Way money is overspent during funerals in the society: i. Buying special funeral clothes. ii. Buying expensive coffins. iii. Preparing special food for mourners - take away/buffet. iv. Keeping corpse in the mortuary for a long time. v. Funeral announcements on the radio and T.V., newspaper/billboards/banners. vi. Employing special undertakers/mourners, pallbearers. vii. Preparing special graves. viii. Expensive entertainment/hiring of expensive venues ix provision of sovenirs

questions.question:
(a) Narrate the circumstances under which Peter was rescued from prison.

(b) Mention any three lessons that can be learnt from the above incident.
questions.explanation: A. Circumstances under which Peter was rescued from prison. (Acts 12:1-19): i.Herod Agrippa joined in the opposition to the gospel by persecuting the disciples to please the Jews. . ii He had James the brother of John killed. iii. After James' death, he realized that the Jews were happy. iv. And in order to please them the more. he had Peter imprisoned. v. Herod's intention was to have Peter killed after the feast of unleavened bread. vi. The night prior to the day Herod planned to kill Peter, Peter was sleeping between two soldiers. vii. Suddenly, an angel of the Lord appeared to Peter and asked him to dress up and put on his shoes. viii. While in prison, fervent prayers were said for Peter by the brethren. ix. The angel commanded Peter to wrap his mantle and follow him. x. Peter followed the angel through the first and second gates. xi. When Peter got to the Iron Gate leading to the City, the gate opened on its own accord. xii. And just as they went out, the angel left Peter and he realized that it was an angel of the Lord that came to rescue him. xiii. Peter went to Mary's house and when knocked at the door, Rhoda saw and she announced his presence to the brethren. xiv However, the brethren did not believe her and thought she was mad. XV. The brethren insisted that it was peters angel that she saw. xvi. Peter then joined the brethren who were praying for him in the house of Mary the mother of John Mark. B Lessons that can be learned from the incident in 7A above: i. The united fervent prayer of the church has a great effect. ii. The church should learn to petition God and intercede for those in crisis. iii. God still answers the prayers of the faithful ones. iv. God can still save his people in any difficult situation. v. We should have no doubt when we pray/believe in our prayers. vi. In every situation, God is still with us. vii. The need to trust in God no matter the circumstance. viii. The supremacy of God prevails over all other authorities.

questions.question:
(a) Explain, in detail, how James addressed the subject of prayer.

(b) Mention at least two roles prayer can play in the life of a Christian.
questions.explanation: A. How James addressed the subịect of prayer (James 1:2-8; 5: 13-18): i. James admonished believers to avoid sin since God detests it so sinners must confess and repent. ii. He encouraged Christians to be joyful in times of trials. iii. According to James, trials, trials are meant to test one's faith. iv. And when one's faith IS fully tested, it produces steadfastness. V. And steadfastness lead to perfection and one lacking nothing. VI. James encouraged those who lack the wisdom to pray to God who gives without reproach. vii. He said prayers should be said in faith without doubt for those who doubt will receive nothing. viii. James compares the one who doubts to the wave of a sea that is driven by the wind. ix. He further said that prayers must be made according to the will of God, x. He also urged Christians to exercise patience when praying for God's will to be done at the right time. xi. James advised Čhristians to pray in humility. xii. He again said that there should be persistence When one prays. xiii. Christians should do away with double-mindedness when praying. xiv. James is of the VIew that anyone suffering should pray, and the cheerful should sing hymns of praise. xv. He again remarked the sick should be anointed with oil and prayed for by the elders xvi From James point of view, prayer made in faith will bring healing to the sick xvii James also staes that a righteous man's prayer has great power in its effects. xviii. in conclusion. James states that Elijah prayed that it should not rain for three and half years and it did not rain. xix. And he again prayed that it should rain and it did B Roles prayer can play in the life of a Christian: i. It helps one to make requests to God. ii. One has the privilege to thank God. iii. One is quipped to fight the devil. İv. Prayer is a source of spiritual strength to lead a good Christian life. v. One's sins can be forgiven through prayer. vi. It gives the believer hope. vii. Through prayer, We commune and fellowship with God. viii. It serves as a medium to adore God.

questions.question:
(a) State in detail, all that Peter expected from the people when he said, "But you are a chosen race, a Royal Priesthood, a holy nation".
(b) Enumerate four factors that prevent Christians from doing the will of God.
questions.explanation: A "But you are a chosen race, a Royal Priesthood, a holy nation"The expectations of Peter from the people in reference to this quote: i. Peter says Christians have been transformed from darkness into light so they should declare the wonderful deeds of God. ii. He said formerly, Christians were no people but they are now God's people who have received mercý. iii. Peter appealed to Christians not to conform to the standards of this world. iv. He admonished them to avoid the passions of the flesh and things that hinder their spiritual growth. v. He was of the view that believers must maintain good conduct among non-Christians so that through their deeds, God will be glorified. vi. Peter holds the view that, Christians are to be subject to every human institution/authority. vii. According to Peter, Christians should not misuse the freedom they have to do evil. viii. The believer, as Peter states, should honour all men. ix. He again states that Christians should love their brothers and fear God. x. The Christian should honour the one who leads him. xi. Peter also admonished servants to submit themselves to their masters. xii. AS a chosen race, Christians are advised by Peter to have patience when they suffer for no wrong done. xiii. He continued that Christians should emulate the example of Christ who suffered for no wrong done. xiv. Finally, Peter encouraged Christians to die to sin and live to righteousness since Christ died on the cross for our sins. B. Factors that prevent Christians from doing the will of God: i.Failure to read the Bible always/ignorance of the word of God. ii. Disobedience to the word of God. iii. Living in sin/immorality. iv. Prayerlessness. V. Negative peer pressure. vi. Unforgiveness/hatred. vii. Persecution. viii. Hostile environment. ix. Religious intolerance. x. Worldliness/materialism/greed. xi. Negative cultural/traditional practices.

questions.question:
Themes From The Old Testament
 
(a) Give an account of the story of the crossing of the Red Sea by the Israelites under the leadership of Moses.
(b) Mention three anc the lessons that can be learnt about the nature of the God from the above incident.
questions.explanation: (Exodus 13:17-22, 14:1-31) (i) Pharaoh allowed the Israelites to leave Egypt into the wilderness to worship God after years resistance, (ii) He thought they would be on a three-day journey as they had earlier requested (iii) Pharaoh never knew that they intended to leave forever, (iv) When Pharaoh was informed that the Israelites had fled, he regretted allowing them to go. (v) Pharaoh the and his men took their chariots and chased ee the Israelites. (vi) God hardened Pharaoh's of heart and he pursued the Israelites till he caught up with them at the Red Sea. (vii) The Israelites feared greatly when the Egyptians were just behind them and Red Sea was before them. (viii) They complained to Moses that he had brought them to the wilderness to die. (ix) The Israelites further said they would have preferred serving the Egyptians in Egypt to dying in the wilderness. (x) Moses encouraged them not to be afraid but to stand firm and see the salvation of the Lord. (xi) they were seeing that day, would never be seen again. (xi) According to Moses, the Lord would fight for them and that they should be still. (xiii) God told Moses to inform the the Israelites not to cry but move forward. (xiv) Moses was asked by the Lord. to lift up his rod and stretch his "hand over the sea (to divide it). (x) The Lord hardened the hearts of the Egyptians so they would go into the sea to catch up with the Israelites. (xvi) At this point, the angel of God who was in front of the Israelites went behind them in the form of a pillar of cloud. (xvii) Moses then stretched out his hand over the sea as commanded and it parted creating a dry land, (xviii) The Israelites then walked on the dry land across the sea to the other side. (xix) The Egyptians chased them through the dry land but Moses stretched his hand, the sea merged killing Pharaoh and his people. (b) Nature of God: (i) God is Omnipresent. (i)God is Omnipotent (iii)Nature responds to God (iv) God is always faithful to his people (v) God provides for his people. (vi) It shows how gracious God is (vi)God is Omniscience. (viii) God protects his people. (ix) It shows the sovereignty of God.

questions.question:
Themes From The Old Testament
(a) Relate the events that led to the Providing pronouncement of punishment on the household of Eli.
(b) State three ways by in their which parents can make their children responsible.
questions.explanation: (a)(1 Sam 2:11-36): (i) Eli, the priest of God had 'two sons; Hophni and Phinehas. (ii) These sons were also priests of God. (iii) However, Eli's sons were worthless men who had no regards for the Lord. (iv) The priest could only take sacrificial meat while it was being boiled. (v) With a three-pronged fork, the servants of the priest would take for himself whatever the fork brought up. (vi) However, the sons of Eli would reject this law and would rather demand raw meat. (vii) Even when their attention was drawn to the law, they would forcefully take whatever portion of meat they wanted. (viii) This sin of Eli's sons was very great in the sight of the lord for they treated the Lord's sacrifice with contempt. (ix) Meanwhile, Samuel, a small boy living with Eli kept the law and was faithfully ministering before the Lord. (x) Eli was well aware of the depraved life of his sons who even slept with the women serving at the entrance of the tent of meeting. (xi) Eli drew the attention of his sons to the enormity of their sins and encouraged them to repent, (xii) However, the sons' of Eli did not listen to their father' rebuke, for it was the Lord's will to put them to death. (xiii) Now, a man of God came to Eli to remind him of the Lord's relationship with Israel and how He chose Eli's father as a priest to serve in His presence.
